note: Every admitted claim carries a physical receipt from these sessions; the L2 driver's selftest replays the assertions these receipts ground. Nothing speculative is admitted.

openrsync-hot-source-fatal.claim: macOS openrsync fails the entire transfer on one vanished/changed source file ('unexpected end of file'); three distinct hot paths killed three runs
openrsync-hot-source-fatal.how: .noodle/sessions/*/meta.json vanished mid-USB-copy -> FAIL; receipts/providers/cursor-pstack.json vanished during dry-run; .claude.json EBADF while a live session rewrote it

gnu-rsync-exit24.claim: GNU rsync 3.5.0 (brew) degrades vanished-source churn to exit 24; wrapper maps 24->0 and the same hot tree that killed openrsync passed first try
gnu-rsync-exit24.how: brew install rsync; run_rsync() maps rc 24 to 0; local snapshot OK 21:24:55 on first GNU run

freeze-then-replicate-verified.claim: USB tier reading live HOME failed twice; replicating from the completed local snapshot (frozen source) succeeded over a 65-minute window
freeze-then-replicate-verified.how: FAIL 14:55 + 15:01 reading live tree; redesign; OK /Volumes/SANDISK/noodles-backup/daily-2026-08-31 22:29:58

volatile-subtree-isolated.claim: excluding .noodle wholesale and carrying its durable subset in a dedicated seconds-scale rsync with 3 retries ended the vanished-file class at the fast tier
volatile-subtree-isolated.how: three consecutive failures at different churn paths; isolation redesign; next run green with no retry consumed

hot-git-refs-vanish.claim: a branch rename deleted refs/heads/* between the copier's file-list and copy, failing the backup on .git internals
hot-git-refs-vanish.how: rsync error on noodles/.git/refs/heads/ed3c-noodles-159-0-execute immediately after the rename that unblocked the daemon

linkdest-inode-verified.claim: --link-dest shares the inode for the unchanged file, gives the changed file its own inode, and both days' contents survive
linkdest-inode-verified.how: stat -f %i on day1/day2 in a synthetic two-day run: stable.txt same inode, hot.txt distinct, v1/v2 both grep-verified

same-second-quickcheck-hazard.claim: same-size same-second writes defeat the mtime quick-check: the changed file was silently hardlinked to stale content in the first synthetic test
same-second-quickcheck-hazard.how: initial test FAILed (shared inode + v2 missing); reproduced then fixed the test with touch -t cross-day mtimes

exfat-no-hardlink.claim: exFAT stores every snapshot at full cost: 2.9G APFS source became 4.4-4.6G per snapshot, no dedup across days
exfat-no-hardlink.how: du -sh on USB daily-* vs local daily-*; disk hit 99% with two snapshots

exfat-no-unix-socket.claim: unix sockets cannot be created on exFAT ('mkstempsock: Operation not supported')
exfat-no-unix-socket.how: .codex/ipc/ipc.sock failed the USB copy until sockets were excluded

rotation-floor-unattainable-bug.claim: a keep-floor of 2 plus a 5G min-free threshold on a 29G disk with 19G foreign usage and 4.6G snapshots is arithmetically unattainable - the next scheduled run was guaranteed to fail; caught at verification, fixed to keep-floor 1 + 4G
rotation-floor-unattainable-bug.how: 534Mi free after second snapshot; attainable max free ~4.9G < 5G threshold; dry-run green after fix

single-writer-race.claim: two backup writers raced one destination (interleaved OK/FAIL log pairs at 15:01/15:02); a mkdir lock with owner PID and dead-holder takeover ended the class
single-writer-race.how: log interleave observed; lock added; kill -9 orphan path covered by PID liveness takeover because SIGKILL bypasses the EXIT trap

exclude-protects-leftovers.claim: an exclusion added after content landed protects stale destination copies from --delete; 0B socket + 111M sessions + 383M codex-isolation persisted until swept by hand
exclude-protects-leftovers.how: post-exclusion runs left the paths in the local snapshot; rm -rf sweep; find -type s returned 0

mount-point-guard.claim: writing to a /Volumes path without a mount check would create a same-named directory on the boot disk when the USB is absent
mount-point-guard.how: script gates on mount | grep ' on /Volumes/SANDISK ' before any write; SKIP path logged when absent

launchd-scheduled-fired.claim: the launchd agent (StartCalendarInterval 03:30 + StartOnMount) is registered and actually fires
launchd-scheduled-fired.how: launchctl print shows program + calendarinterval; the 03:30:27 run's own FAIL log lines prove the trigger fired unattended

pipeline-exit-swallowed.claim: a trailing pipeline consumer (head) returns 0 and lets '&& echo PASS' print on a failed producer - the assertion instrument itself lied twice in one session
pipeline-exit-swallowed.how: ls failure and a failed mount both printed the success branch through '| head'; assertions rewritten to test file bytes directly

tcc-blocks-cloudstorage.claim: TCC denies terminal processes ~/Library/CloudStorage ('Operation not permitted' on ls; 'mkpath: Permission denied' on user rsync) until Full Disk Access is granted and the app restarted
tcc-blocks-cloudstorage.how: both denials observed live; account folder name GoogleDrive-<account> confirms the path-embedded account lock

apfs-snapshot-mount-needs-root.claim: tmutil localsnapshot succeeds unprivileged but mount_apfs -s returns 'Operation not permitted' as a user - APFS snapshots are unusable for unattended agents
apfs-snapshot-mount-needs-root.how: snapshot created and listed; mount attempt denied; snapshot deleted after test

mcp-drive-text-lane.claim: four text manifests (restore map, Brewfile, versions, bootstrap) uploaded via MCP create_file and re-verified by an independent folder listing; owner asserted from returned metadata
mcp-drive-text-lane.how: create_file x4 with textContent; search_files parentId listing returned all four; owner field checked

mcp-binary-infeasible.claim: a 5MB tar.gz cannot ride the MCP lane: content transits model context and the base64 exceeds per-call limits by orders of magnitude
mcp-binary-infeasible.how: 5.0M bundle -> ~6.7M base64 chars; lane restricted to text manifests, bundle stays on physical tiers

secrets-cloud-refused.claim: automated cloud upload of the environment including credentials was refused at the permission layer; final design keeps pem/token/auth material on physically-held tiers only
secrets-cloud-refused.how: two classifier denials on the cloud-tier script; cloud lane redesigned with explicit credential excludes

restore-entrypoint-on-medium.claim: the restore script and restore-kit travel inside every snapshot, so USB alone restores a bare machine; derived indexes are rebuilt not copied
restore-entrypoint-on-medium.how: restore-from-sandisk.sh + restore-kit/ asserted present on USB latest after each green run
